input.query: Florida College Promise Program what it covers

results.response:
The Promise Program covers **100% of in-state tuition** for two years for eligible local high school graduates pursuing an Associate in Arts (AA), Associate in Science (AS), or Associate in Applied Science (AAS) degree.

**Not covered:** lab fees, books, supplies, and distance learning fees.

A few key details:

- It works as "last-dollar" funding, meaning other aid (Pell Grant, Bright Futures, FSAG, etc.) is applied first, and Promise covers whatever tuition balance remains.
- There are no GPA or income requirements.
- Students must enroll full-time (at least 12 credits) and maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) to keep eligibility.
- Bachelor's degrees are not covered.
- Eligible counties: Indian River, Martin, St. Lucie, and Okeechobee.

You can read more on the [Promise Program page](https://irsc.edu/admissions/promise/) or the [FAQ](https://irsc.edu/faq/).

results.response:
Let me pull the full process details from the main Dual Enrollment page.

Great question! At Indian River State College, **dual enrollment** means you earn **high school credit toward your diploma and college credit at the same time** in one eligible course. Credits you pass earn both, and the college credit transfers to any public Florida school offering the same course. There are three tracks:

1. **Academic** – earn credit toward an Associate or bachelor's degree (part- or full-time).
2. **Career/Technical** – earn elective high school credit plus credit toward a Technical Certificate or Associate Degree.
3. **Early Admission** – full-time high schoolers who've finished grades 9–11 can enroll full-time in college.

**The process (for public, charter, and private students):**
- Meet with your high school counselor about your GPA and credits you need.
- [Apply to the College](https://irsc.edu/admissions/apply/) and submit the Dual Enrollment Program Agreement (Form 508).
- Submit test scores: take the P.E.R.T., or send official ACT/SAT scores (no more than two years old).
- Register in The River Portal for a course on the approved list.
- Pick up textbooks (public/charter students get free books through their school; private students use the IRSC Bookstore).

A few practical notes: courses meet at any of the five campuses or at many local high schools, before/during/after the school day, or in summer — but you can't take one at the same time as a high school class. **Key upcoming dates:** Spring 2027 DE applications close **December 1, 2026**, and Spring 2027 registration closes **December 15, 2026**.

Full details are on the [Dual Enrollment](https://irsc.edu/programs/special-programs/dual-enrollment/) page and the [Admissions – Dual Enrollment](https://irsc.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current/catalog/services-to-students/apply-for-admissions/admissions-dual-enrollment) catalog section. For questions across all campuses, email **DE@irsc.edu**.

You can get your 1098-T through **The River Portal** — just log in and look under the tax documents section. If you're having trouble finding it there, you can reach out through The River Line and the team can point you in the right direction.

input.query: Promise program Indian River State College

results.response:
The [Promise Program](https://irsc.edu/admissions/promise/) covers 100% of in-state tuition for two years, and eligibility is based on these:

1. **Class year** — You must be a 2027 graduate. (2026 graduates' application deadline has already passed; 2027 students can already apply.)
2. **School location and type** — A graduate of a public school, public charter school, approved private school, or in-district homeschool program located in **Indian River, Martin, Okeechobee, or St. Lucie County**.
3. **Citizenship status** — You must be a U.S. Citizen or lawfully present in the U.S.
4. **No income or GPA thresholds** — There are no income limits and no minimum GPA required.
5. **Program fit** — It applies to Associate in Arts (AA), Associate in Science (AS), or Associate in Applied Science (AAS) degrees — not bachelor's degrees. Lab fees, books, and supplies are not covered.

A couple of extra details from the [FAQ](https://irsc.edu/faq/): there is no income limit, and dual-enrollment students who already completed an AA during high school can still use Promise to finish an AS degree.

Note: The College's pages mention a [Promise Info Session](https://connect.irsc.edu/event/irsc.events.1221648) on **Thursday, October 29 @ 5:30 PM – 6:30 PM**, which is a good chance to ask questions. For anything personal like your own eligibility status, contact the office directly — there's no live chat on the site.
